subject: Terms of Use
author: ZombieTron
body:
The comments were closed as several comments were against the Terms of Use.

Although, there is some leniance on comments where we are aware of the relationship between the members and know that there is no offence taken or received, not everybody who reads the comments know that there is no harm and may copy the sentiments thinking that if it is allowed by one, it should be allowed by all.

OK my point! Flame wars are not tolerated, even if Nero and GT are just flaming each other it reflects on the content of the site as a whole and we do like to try to keep the content slightly higher then the gutter, please refrain from pointless flaming, I think that is what the xbox.com forums are for! 🙂

Please use the PM's and not the comments to reply personally to individual members. Also, please do not use drug references. I have edited your GT comment. Please try to keep your comments family friendly.

subject: I prefer 7-up!
author: ZombieTron
body:
But, I do like the flavour of both. 🙂

I don't want to restart anything here as Xandu locking down the comments on the thread in question was the right thing to do, but I will say that the negative response was due to you ripping the ssip out of one of our longstanding members and friends, and not really anything to do with console wars.

That being said, welcome to BurnoutAholics and I hope you continue to post here, following ofcourse our terms of use.

Up until PS2/Xbox I always owned every console, I had a snes and a megadrive, a saturn and an N64, a Dreamcast, gamecube and a PS1. I think the main difference with this generation is online play and cost, both the PS3 and Xbox 360 seem to me to be much more significant investments then previous generations, and with online play I think people are more likely to pick one system and stick to that one, then to have both. Trying to play with 2 different friends lists on 2 different consoles will take a lot of time and juggling. I think the fact that we have friends lists, friends in fact who share the love of the same console as us also leads to people being a little defensive, as it is more than just a console now.. it is a community.

The Burnout community should transcend console differences, platform differences even as we also include hand-held and PC gamers. Whatever platform you play Burnout on, you are welcome here! 🙂

subject: Mostly Agree
author: Abernyte
body:
Speaking as a PS3 user, I think you'll find just as many PS3 fanboys as XBox fanboys so I don't know that it's fair to characterize it as a XBox issue. Let's be honest, you'll find jerks on both systems. But your underlying point is dead on - it shouldn't matter or be a basis of dictating whose opinion matters.

Almost everything I've seen on BA tells me the site is intended to be inclusive; XBox, PS3, noob, experienced, Paradise or Revenge, etc. That is one of the appeals of the site. It doesn't try to be exclusive and doesn't have the holier than thou attitude of some sites. I think it's a lot harder to maintain a site like that than it is some of the free for alls that allow personal insults and general idiocy.

Instances of personal attacks and elitism are pretty rare here. Hopefully we can keep it that way.
